summary: A command or a short piece of code in IBM Plex Mono, with a copy button on the same line. The button says Copied for two seconds, so the reader knows the paste will work.
whenToUse: A command the reader runs or pastes: an install line, an MCP server setup, a CLI call.
A short snippet the reader copies as is: a CSS variable in use, an import line.
Keep commands on one line (the default): a long command scrolls inside the block, so it stays one command. Turn on wrap for prose-like code the reader reads more than pastes.
hideCopy for code the reader should read, not paste: a file path, an example output.
Plain-script pages that build rows as HTML strings use codeBlockHtml() and bindCodeBlocks() from @bridge-ds/react/dom: the same markup and the same copy behavior, without React.
whenNotToUse: A token name or value inside a sentence or a table cell: use TokenValue.
A whole file or a long diff: link to it, or show it in a dedicated viewer.
Inline code in running text: use the code element of the page's prose styles.

dos.title: Name what the code does
dos.text: A short label above the block (Install, Add the MCP server) tells the reader which block to copy, and names the copy button for screen readers: Copy install.

dos.title: One command per block
dos.text: Two steps are two blocks, each with its own label and copy button. The reader pastes one thing at a time and sees which one worked.

donts.title: A prompt sign in the code
donts.text: The block copies exactly what it shows. A leading $ ends up in the terminal and the command fails.

donts.title: Several commands chained in one block
donts.text: A row of commands joined with && is hard to read and fails as a whole. Split it into one block per step.

p.label: Set up
p.code: npm install @bridge-ds/react && npx @bridge-ds/cli init && npx @bridge-ds/cli publish

accessibility: The copy button is a real Button. With a string label it is named Copy plus the label (Copy install); after a copy it reads Copied.
A polite live region announces Copied to the clipboard. If the clipboard is blocked, the code is selected and the region says to press Ctrl+C or Cmd+C.
A block that does not wrap is keyboard focusable (tabindex 0), so a long line can be scrolled with the arrow keys. A wrapped block needs no focus stop.

Copy works without hydration: statically rendered blocks carry data-code-block hooks and bindCodeBlocks() from @bridge-ds/react/dom wires them. Plain scripts render the same markup with codeBlockHtml().
Code text uses color.text.default on color.bg.subtle, checked in both themes.
contentGuidelines: Label: what the code does, sentence case, no period: "Install", "Add the MCP server".
Code: exactly what the reader pastes. No prompt sign, no placeholder the reader has to spot and replace without being told.
When a value must be replaced, say so in the text above the block and name the value: "Replace acme/design-tokens with your repository".
